move: circular lens wanders a blurred UI, opening sharp windows, then closes
how: Two identical copies of a settings UI card sit on a dark stage with a purple glow: the lower copy is blurred (filter blur 18px) under a frosted panel, the upper copy is sharp but clipped by clip-path circle(r at x y). Header lines and a footer rise out of masks (expo.out) and the blurred panel lifts in from y 60 over the first 14%. From 14% a lens object visits five stops: it travels (x/y, expo.inOut 0.9s), opens (r from 0 to 130-210px, back.out(1.6) 0.6s) while a ring element scales with it, holds 0.5s (0.9s on the last centred stop), then closes (r to 0, expo.in 0.45s), each stop taking ~2.1s. The UI copies drift up 14px and back over the loop, and two switches flip on at 52%. At 92% the header, footer and blurred panel push out.
adapt: Replace the UI markup (rendered into both copies), the header/footer copy, the stop coordinates and radii, and the accent gradient. Keep the 0.9s expo.inOut travel, 0.6s back.out opening and 0.45s expo.in close.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the glow, header, both UI copies, frost, lens ring and footer inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline; the lens proxy tweens with onUpdate apply must write clip-path on the sharp layer inside el, with stop coordinates relative to el.
caveats: filter: blur(18px) on a full card plus blur(30px) on the glow, slow to render
clip-path circle updated every frame via onUpdate
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late
